From: Michael Sullivan <michael.sullivan@amazon.com>

Cc: AWS Partner Sales <aws-partner-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer request for CloudValley — commission and SKU mapping

Vanessa,

Quick intro — I’m Michael Sullivan on the AWS ISV partner team. CloudValley (procurement copied) is evaluating Redwood as a primary inference stack for a new analytics product across AWS and potentially multi-cloud. They want to buy via an AWS private offer.

They’ve asked us a few questions we need your help to answer so we can get a private-offer packaged quickly:
- What is Redwood’s standard private-offer discount vs list for AWS? Do you have a discount matrix by committed ARR or term?
- Does Redwood support split billing / channel commission (i.e., a reseller margin carved out of the private-offer price)? If so, what % ranges are typical and what requires exec approval?
- Can you provide SKU mapping for a bundle we can use in the private offer (monthly recurring compute + per-token usage)?
- Any constraints on minimum ACV or allowed resale discounts for marketplace SKUs?

I’ve attached the CloudValley procurement sheet they filled out (draft-private-offer-reqs.xlsx). Would love to align on numbers this week — CloudValley is asking for an indicative private-offer by EOW.

Thanks,
Michael Sullivan
AWS ISV Partner
Amazon Web Services

Attachment: draft-private-offer-reqs.xlsx (43 KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private offer request for CloudValley — commission and SKU mapping

Michael — thanks for the intro and the procurement sheet. Looping in Karthik (sales), Marissa (finance/partnerships review), and Logan (marketplace team) so we can pull together an indicative construct.

Quick answers up front so CloudValley has something to work with while we sync:
- We typically publish a private-offer discount band (list price delta) that scales with committed ARR and term — typical starting discounts are 12–18% off list for 12–24 month commitments. Heavier discounts (20%+) require a commercial approval and minimum commit.
- We support channel split mechanics in private offers, but commission >12% usually needs finance/partnership sign-off. We can do an element of reseller carve-out inside the offer or manage via separate billing depending on partner preference.
- SKU mapping: we can produce a SKU bundle for compute reservation + per-token metering; Logan, can you draft a quick SKU mapping for the CloudValley profile?

Karthik — can you propose an initial channel margin and approach (private-offer list discount vs reseller carve)? Also suggest if we need any approval path shortened for this account — they’re sensitive to timing.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Thanks Vanessa / Michael — below is a proposed starting point for discussion (open to adjustments):

Proposal (indicative):
- List discount (private offer): 18% off list with a 12-month committed ARR (preferred). If customer commits 24 months / higher ARR, move to 20–22% band.
- Channel commission: 8–10% standard carve (paid to reseller/partner). If partner requests >12% channel commission, require Marissa’s approval and a revenue-impact sign-off.
- SKU mapping approach: create a bundled SKU for 1) reserved inference capacity (monthly recurring) and 2) token overage (metered). Will provide a lightweight mapping file to AWS for the private-offer draft.
- Minimum ACV: $50k ARR preferred for private offers that include channel commission; below that we can evaluate on a case-by-case basis.

Risks / asks for AWS / CloudValley:
- If CloudValley insists on a 20%+ discount plus a 10% channel commission, that materially compresses Redwood’s unit economics. We can consider a phased approach: start with a 12-month pilot with lower committed volume, then expand pricing on renewal.
- Need clarity on whether CloudValley will want the reseller to invoice or be included as a carve in the private-offer pricing. If included, AWS billing rules and marketplace reconciliation times will apply.

I attached a template we use for private offers that maps SKUs to pricing lines — send me any changes and I’ll finalize.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_AWS_Private_Offer_Template_v2.docx (58 KB)

Karthik / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround. Two follow-ups from CloudValley:
1) They are pushing for a 20% private-offer discount off list.
2) They’d like the reseller commission at 10% (paid as a carve from the private-offer MSRP).

CloudValley is flexible on a 12-month term but needs the economic to be within a tight band because they have internal reseller margins to preserve. They asked whether Redwood would accept a 20% discount + 10% reseller carve if we do a staged delivery (pilot month metrics and then formal renewal pricing). They also requested that we provide explicit SKU lines so AWS can draft the private offer.

Michael

Karthik — flagged a few constraints from finance/ops:
- Channel commission: up to 12% can be approved through Partnerships. Anything >12% requires VP Finance + CFO approval and a formal commercial memo detailing unit economics and churn exposure. Expect a 7–10 business day review cycle for expedited requests.
- Combined discount + commission: if the private-offer list discount exceeds 18% AND a commission >10% is requested, we need to model 36 months of revenue and request a one-time pricing exception. That’s a >2 week path.
- Minimum ACV tied to fiscal recognition: for private offers with channel carve-outs, we prefer ACV >= $75k to avoid disproportionate reconciliation overhead.

Operational asks: please provide the pricing-workbook-cloudvalley.csv with the SKU lines and expected monthly usage so ops can validate billing reconciliation in AWS. If CloudValley is insistent on the 20%+ discount plus 10% carve, we can propose a pilot agreement (3-month pilot at limited volume) to mitigate risk and reprice on renewal.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

Michael / CloudValley — appreciate the clear ask. Short answer: we can do a 20% private-offer discount paired with a 10% channel carve, but not on a standard automated approval path. Proposed path to keep momentum:

1) Pilot + staged economics (recommended)
   - 3-month pilot at reduced committed capacity (defined in the pricing workbook). During pilot we honor a 20% off-list discount with a 10% reseller carve.
   - If pilot metrics meet agreed thresholds (token throughput, latency, platform integration), we convert to a 12-month contract re-evaluated at renewal pricing.

2) Commercial approvals (parallel)
   - Karthik / Marissa to file a short commercial memo to Finance summarizing the pilot economics and strategic rationale (partner motion + likely ARR expansion). We’ll aim for expedited review (7 business days) with Jonas as backup approver if needed.

3) SKU lines & DocuSign
   - Logan to deliver the SKU mapping to Michael by EOD tomorrow so AWS can draft the private offer.
   - Once we have final lines, we’ll provide a DocuSign-ready commercial addendum.

If CloudValley accepts the staged approach we can keep to their EOW timeline for an indicative private offer. If they require a firm 12-month commitment at the proposed economics up front, we’ll need a slightly longer approval path.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
